newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty climbs as currencies flood market, T/N rise.
newsitem.headline: Zloty climbs as currencies flood market, T/N rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty jumped some 0.3 percentage point against the basket of currencies as a large supply of currencies pushed the local unit higher in active trade on Monday, dealers said.

They were mixed whether the currency-selling trend was connected with foreign entry in Polish T-bills, shortening of currency positions due to low liquidity on the money market or inflows from privatisation deals.
"There were large-scale currency sales but they were likely the result of domestic factors, such as a zloty-dry (money) market," said Malgorzata Sawicka from Bank Handlowy SA.

Some dealers said foreigners may have bought large amounts of currencies on Monday to purchase T-bills at today's 1.1 billion zloty primary tender or pay for recently bought 16-percent two-year bonds, whose value date is December 5.

"Foreigners may have entered the Polish market and if so the zloty should stay underpinned at high levels at least until Tuesday, because tomorrow/next foreign exchange transactions may be done," said one foreign dealer bank here.
Others said the large amount of currencies on the market stemmed from a privatisation deal, but treasury ministry could not immidiately confirm any pending sell-off inflows.

The zloty closed at 2.43/2.40 percent from the trading band centre on Monday, stronger from Friday's close at 2.13/2.06 percent. It was at 2.8485/95 per dollar, down from 2.8475/85 on Friday and at 1.8460/66 to the mark, up from 1.8560/75.

One-day deposit rates rose on the money market, as players searched for zlotys to repay short-term funds borrowed before the end of November's reserve period. Players also wanted to keep monthly reserve positions balanced in December.
"Banks want to keep reserve positions squared from the start of December becuse of large ouflows near the end of the month," said Maciej Ratulowski from Bank Zachodni SA.
Overnight rates were at 19.70/20.00 percent, up from opening's 19.65/19.80 percent. Tomorrow/next depos were at 19.80/20.00 percent, up from 19.75/20.20 percent.

The ministry sold 669 million zlotys of Polish T-bills on total demand of 1.21 billion zlotys against a 1.1 billion offer, minimum prices remained flat except 52-week paper, whose minimum price fell by one grosz to 83.47.
Demand for shortest paper jumped by 414 million zlotys from the last auction, most likely on non-banking client bids. The average yield for the paper rose by 0.04 to 18.77 percent.
